title: Fort Témiscamingue Chief Factor’s House
geometryBasis: The government management plan places the factor’s house near the west shore in the southwestern group. The south-of-forge OSM house ruins match that relationship and show a central house outline plus a narrower north projection. The unnamed feature is an approximate cross-identification.
sectionBasis: Roy identifies the 1888 house, rear wing and central covered passage. The surviving chimney is independently documented.
limitations: The written archaeology identifies a principal residence and a rear block linked by a central passage. The current house ruin footprint matches that arrangement approximately. The 1888 catalog pose and anteroom dimensions are estimates.
The mapped shape suggests a shorter porch on the south face. Its shape, timber details, roof pitch, storey heights and window arrangement are reconstructed.
The lower western threshold uses the current Terrarium grade reference. The eastern slope and taller rear footing approximate contact with the unchanged modern terrain.
The published 1876 view supports the post’s pale principal timber buildings and massing. The surviving chimney is identified in the regional archaeological guide.
